title: Decode: low-latency dense GEMM family (BF16 + MXFP8)
shape: NVFP4 checkpoint, D3-32 r24 1-node DP-rank slice (24-layer view k31-nvfp4-view-L24, u132k, k=3): R = 384 gathered rows (attention projections), n = 96 shard rows (MoE dense GEMMs) per GPU; per decode step, exposed time
basis: MEASURED in-step (NVFP4 decode baseline, INFRA measured/20261118-1900-nvfp4-decode.json, run rhea runs/INFRA/step_d/trial-9ccf8ab-nv-r8r16r24-prof, overlay trial-9ccf8ab-1 = int b31121cf56 + d-moe). Family = fam.py 'BF16 dense GEMMs' groups (KDA in/o_proj, DSA qkv_a/g/o/w_uv, router+latent_down, latent_up, shared gate_up/down, dense layer). achievable = nvfp4_modelopt model_rows_L24 for the same groups. r8 / r16 rows: 1.201 / 1.311 exposed vs 0.753 / 0.778 achievable.
gap_analysis: Per precision at r24 (exposed vs achievable, us per L24 step): MXFP8 (KDA in/o_proj, shared gate_up/down, quant kernels counted elsewhere) 746 vs 411; BF16 (DSA qkv_a/g/o/w_uv, router+latent_down, latent_up, dense layer) 835 vs 410. Every op in-step is a cuBLAS nvjet kernel (MXFP8: nvjet qqtst Avec32UE8M0). Per call (busy) vs model: KDA in_proj 17.8 vs 7.6 us (92 MB -> 5.2 TB/s), KDA o_proj 7.3 vs 2.1, router+latent_down 3 kernels 20 vs 4.9 (router on main and latent down on aux stream), latent_up 7.4 vs 3.8, DSA qkv_a 15.9 vs 3.4, g_proj 27.6 vs 4.6 (busy, half exposed), DSA o_proj 9.6 vs 4.6, shared down 14.0 vs 3.5 (side stream beside MegaMoE). Root cause: generic library tiles stream weights at 3-7 TB/s (too few bytes in flight per SM, many CTAs per weight byte, separate split-K reduce kernels, no weight prefetch across kernel boundaries); the model streams at 13.9 TB/s striped.
inefficiencies: cuBLAS nvjet tiles stream weights at 3-7 TB/s vs 13.9 striped / ~18 die-local [in-step kernels, gap.json]
separate split-K reduce launches (nvjet splitK variants: router, dense layer) [gap.json kernel names]
no weight prefetch across kernel boundaries: each GEMM pays launch + ramp + grid-end drain (~3-4 us) [hwdb launch costs; bench1 small-weight floor]
MXFP8 activation quant as separate kernels before each MXFP8 GEMM [bench1]
x re-read per 128-row weight tile at R=384 (3x the weight bytes from L2) unless x is shared across CTAs [design analysis]
rubin_features: tcgen05 MMA swap-AB (weights M128, tokens N), TMEM accumulators, 2 segments per CTA
TMA 128B-swizzled boxes, L2 evict_first on streamed weights
1 CTA per SM, whole shared memory as the weight ring
PDL: weight boxes requested before griddepcontrol.wait, launch_dependents at entry
planned: cluster TMA multicast of the token box (R=384), die-local weight homing + per-die chunks, kind::mxf8f6f4 2x-K with in-kernel activation quant, oversized shared memory
plan: SOL design (recorded 19:15): one persistent stream-K kernel per GEMM, 1 CTA/SM, equal weight bytes per SM (K-block chunks spanning <= 2 tiles), swap-AB tcgen05 M128 x N=R with TMEM accumulators, weight ring = whole smem (~128 KB+ weights in flight per SM), split tiles reduced through L2 in the same kernel (each contributor sums its token share in contributor order: deterministic, one rounding), PDL weight prefetch before the dependency wait so HBM stays busy across GEMM boundaries. Bound: weight bytes / HBM rate (13.9 striped, ~18 die-local) + ~1 us tail per GEMM. Projected r24 family: ~0.85-0.90 ms striped (<= target 0.90), ~0.75 die-local.
1. BF16 kernel stream_gemm (R <= 256) + microbench at D3-32 shapes vs cuBLAS chained cold weights [in progress]
2. R = 384: 2 accumulators of N=192 + token box shared across a 2-CTA cluster (multicast) to keep L2 x traffic <= weight bytes
3. MXFP8 variant: kind::mxf8f6f4 (sm_107a 2x-K), weight SF via tcgen05.cp, activation quant fused in the producer path (drops the separate quant kernels)
4. router + latent_down as one GEMM over the concatenated weight (same input); beta-add epilogue for latent_up
5. die-local weights (common/dies.py localized allocation) + die-aware chunk assignment by %smid
6. wire into sdec (DecodeProjection kind 'stream', Mxfp8Projection), unit tests, step_d A/B on int overlay, landed-ready
